column1: # Prewarm seed list (shipped in the app, next to shader_map.tsv). Rows: S<TAB>shader key<TAB>stage / R<TAB>render pipeline key (pso_skey hex) / C<TAB>compute shader key.

# Recorded on the Mac (DM_PSO_RECORD, prewarm off) over update 1.9.0: boot → title → New Game → the Shrine of Resurrection until Link can move; then boot → title → a save load (Zora's Domain) and a minute of play, its new lines appended. 960 render pipelines + 819 shaders + 10 compute shaders. Row order = first-use order; do not sort.

# Then, below the Mac rows and their own note, an iPhone 18 Pro Max's Documents/pso_user.tsv from the owner's play on 0.5 (update 1.9.0): the rows the Mac list did not hold, 4467 rows: 4070 S, 392 R, 5 C. In all 6256 rows: 4889 S, 1352 R, 15 C.

# Recorded on an iPhone 18 Pro Max from the owner's play on 0.5 (5b302cd0, chain ac67cb709fa0, update 1.9.0 v1114112), Frame rate 60 (the frame step), Picture Stretch, no upscaling, no edge smoothing: Documents/pso_user.tsv after the first start of a fresh install (an empty device archive; the rows above prepared before the first frame) and about 3:50 from boot (12,000 frames), which records only the rows the list above did not hold, 4467 rows: 4070 S, 392 R, 5 C.

# The frame step and Picture Stretch change no pipeline: the stretch is the host's present, the game's render targets keep their sizes and formats (window textures 1920x1080, screen shape 16:9 on this phone), and a row's pipeline key (pso_skey) holds no picture size. Row order = first-use order; do not sort. Checked with dm/tools/pso_seed.py check.
